name: Week 30 Push — The Press Goes First, and the Cable Block Gets the Spotlight
description:
**The press runs first this week and every week from now on.** Last time a free bench moved it to the end and 50 went from three clean strict sets to not being able to strict a single rep of set two. Nothing about the lift got worse — it was asked to run on an empty tank. It leads the day.

**Incline holds 60 and the eccentric goes to 3 seconds.** Twelve reps on all three sets is the top of the range, so tempo is the lever before load is.

**Dips hold 10-12 with the full 2-minute rest and add a 1-second pause at the bottom.** **Lateral raise holds 20**, **farmer carry runs two walks at 60 per hand**, and the cable block takes the spotlight.

dayOverview.theme: Same short day, one structural rule and two tempo levers. The strict press leads because it has to. Incline and dips hold their loads and get slower instead of heavier. The cable block, which has run on autopilot for a month, gets the deep cues.

spotlights.why: It has run at 120 for four weeks without a single note about how it felt. A straight-arm pulldown is easy to turn into a half-triceps movement without noticing — this week the cue is the fixed elbow angle.
The other half of a block that never gets attention, and the one lift with a nerve-line history on the right arm. Worth running deliberately rather than as the thing between the raise and the carry.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W31 — spotlight returns to the strict press, now that it has had a month running from the front. W32 — chest press machine and the Kinesis lateral raise come back when the week stops being short.
watchpoints: 🛑 keep it shy — the cue is the cap: strict DB press, incline DB press, dips, straight-arm pulldown, farmer carry. Effort here means the cue holding at a hard load; the ceiling is the rep the cue breaks.
🔥 near-failure last set OK: DB lateral raise, lean-back cable tricep pushdown. Isolation work where form holds at the limit.

**⭐ THE STRICT PRESS GOES FIRST.** Standing overhead at 50 per hand has no bench holding your torso up — it needs a fresh trunk and fresh delts. **If a busy gym forces it late, write it off as a push press and use leg drive** rather than discovering mid-set that you cannot strict it.
**Take the full 2 minutes on dips.** Same load, same reps, and it is what let the slow tempo survive all three sets.
**Pack DOWN, not up** on every pressing lift. Blades into the back pockets, neck long, traps quiet. A rep that needs a shrug is over.
**No straps on the carry.** If the left hand goes early, set them down, rest, and finish the time — a broken walk is still the work.

**Sleep is still the variable.** If the night was brutal, drop a set from the pressing lifts rather than shortening a single eccentric. That worked last time and it is the instruction, not a concession.

sets.name: Warmup + Shoulder Rehab (Non-Negotiable) + Chest Opener + Protective Shrug
sets.notes: The whole block, every push day. Yuri's band work is the shoulder anchor — it is why the right shoulder has stayed quiet through a heavy pressing block, so it does not get skipped on a short morning.

exercises.notes: Small to large. Just moving blood.
**The shoulder anchor.** Full sequence, light band, no rushing. Cuff first, then scap.

Light bell, inverted. **Wrist stacked over elbow over shoulder** — the bell tipping is the feedback. It rehearses the exact packed-down lockout the press is about to ask for, and today the press is the very next thing you do.
Light. This is the chest opener, not a working set.
Tight fists, thumbs tucked, hinged slightly forward. Wakes the deep core — the press needs the trunk before it needs the shoulders.
Elbows ~45°, **pack down not up.** One easy set.
Greasing set, nowhere near failure. Keeps the pattern alive on a push day.
**Protective activation — before anything loaded.** 40-50lb pair, behind the back, straight up and down.

sets.name: Strict DB Press — 50, First Lift of the Day 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 50lb pair, 3 sets of 6-8. **2 minutes between sets, reps as singles.**

**This is the first loaded lift of the session. Not second, not after dips.**

- **No dip, no knee bend.** The set ends when strict form ends
- **Slow eccentric on every rep**
- **Ribs DOWN at lockout** — no rib flare to get under the weight
- **Pack DOWN, not up.** If the shoulders climb toward the ears, the set is over

**Reflection:** three clean strict sets at 50 from the front — how did that compare to running it last week on an empty tank?

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 50lb pair, 3 sets. 2 min rest, reps as singles.
- **Strict — no leg drive**
- **Slow eccentric every rep**
- Shoulders packed **DOWN**, traps relaxed, ribs down
- If the rack forces this late in the day, run it as a push press instead

sets.name: Incline DB Press — 60, Eccentric Goes to 3s 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 60lb pair, 3 sets of 8-12. **The eccentric goes from 2s to 3s.** 2 minutes between sets.

Twelve reps on all three sets is the top of the range, so the descent gets longer before the dumbbells get heavier.

- **Bench at 30°, not 45°**
- **3s eccentric on every rep** — this is the progression
- **Blades DOWN and BACK into the bench**, chest tall
- **Elbows around 45° from the torso**, not flared to 90
- Stop when the eccentric shortens or the shoulders shrug

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 60lb pair, all 3 sets.
- **30° bench**
- **3s eccentric every rep** — up from 2s
- Blades down and back, ribs down
- 2 min rest, reps as singles

sets.name: Dips — 10-12, Full 2 Minutes, 1s Pause at the Bottom 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** bodyweight, 3 sets of 10-12 on the **angled / V bar**. **2 minutes between sets — take all of it.**

**New this week: a 1-second pause at the bottom of every rep.** Twelve reps got easier across the sets last time, so the bottom position gets held instead of the range getting longer.

- **Rotate the left forearm outward before taking bodyweight** so the pressure sits on the firm inside edge of the hand, not the thumb pad
- Mini-dips against the bar to set the forward lean before rep 1
- **3s descent, then 1s still at the bottom** — shorten the set rather than rush either
- **Pack DOWN at the top.** No shrugging up to lock out
- Sit down between sets

exercises.notes:
Bodyweight, 3 sets. **Angled / V bar. 2 min rest.**
- Set the rotated palm position **before** the first rep
- **3s descent, 1s pause at the bottom**
- Hold the forward lean
- Shoulders packed down at lockout

sets.name: DB Lateral Raise — 20, Tempo Is the Lever 🔥
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 20lb pair, 3 sets of 12-15. If the 20s are taken, run 15 with the tempo intact — the tempo is what earned the load.

All three sets held at 20 last week where set 3 used to die halfway. **If all three sets hit a clean 15 this week, the 25s are the next step.**

- **Slow up, slow down, 1s hold at the top**
- **Lead with the elbows**, little fingers a touch high
- **Traps quiet.** If the shoulders ride up to start the rep, the weight is winning
- Last set may run near failure — safe isolation work

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 20lb pair (15 if the 20s are taken).
- Slow up / slow down / **1s hold**
- Lead with the elbow
- **Traps relaxed** — no shrug to start the rep
- Three clean sets of 15 means 25 next week

sets.name: 🔆 Cable Block — Straight-Arm Pulldown → Lean-Back Tricep Pushdown (2 Rounds)
sets.notes:
**Two rounds, circuit style, minimal rest between the two moves.** Both live on the cable stations — take whichever is free and stay there.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — this block has run on autopilot for a month, so today it gets run deliberately.** Both moves are easy to do adequately and hard to do well, and the failure mode for each is the same: a joint that was supposed to stay still starts moving.

**Reflection:** on the pulldown, could you feel the lats start the movement — or did it feel like triceps? And did the right-arm nerve line stay quiet on the extension?

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:**
- Cable column: **120**
- Rope pulley: **62.5**
- Kinesis: **6**
Pick whichever is free; **note the equipment and number in the log.**

🔆 **The elbow angle is the whole lift:**
- **Set a soft elbow bend and never change it** — if the elbow opens and closes, it has quietly become a triceps pushdown
- **Start the rep by pulling the upper arm down from the armpit**, not by pushing the hands
- Finish with the hands at the thighs, **lats squeezed, ribs down**
- **No leaning back to add range** — the torso angle is fixed too
- Slow return, and let the arms travel all the way up to a real stretch

**LOAD:** cable column **60**, with **50** as the tired-day fallback.

🔆 **The upper arm is the thing that stays still:**
- Torso leans back; hands travel from near the chest to straight arms **by the hips**
- **Elbows stay pinned in space — only the forearms move.** If the elbows drift forward on the way up, the lift has become a pushdown
- **Nothing goes behind the head** — that position is what the right arm dislikes
- **Pack the shoulders down before every set**, and keep them down as the arms straighten
- **Squeeze at full extension**, slow back
- If the right-arm nerve line returns and does not clear, stop the set

sets.name: Farmer Carry — 60 per Hand, Two Walks That Both Hold 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 60lb per hand, 2 walks of ~50s. **No straps.**

Last week ran 50 at the end of a session where the press had already emptied you. With the press at the front this time, 60 is the number again.

- **Crush the handles from the first step** rather than letting the grip fade into it
- **Shoulders packed down**, ribs stacked over hips, walk tall
- The job is two walks that both hold, not a heavier bell
- If the left goes early, set them down, rest, and finish the time

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 60lb per hand. No straps.
- **Grip hard from the first step**
- Shoulders down, ribs stacked, tall posture
- Two walks that hold beats a heavier bell

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block
sets.notes: Five minutes, every gym day. Slow breathing throughout — the downshift is as much the point as the tissue.

exercises.notes: 30s each arm, elbow at MID height.
Passive. Let the shoulders decompress.
30s each side.
45s each side.
Slow breathing. End here.

tips: The press is the first loaded lift. If the rack is busy, wait for it rather than reordering the day.
Incline stays at 60 — the 3s descent is this week's progression.
Dips add a 1s pause at the bottom. Still the full 2 minutes between sets.
Log which cable station you used and the number on that station's scale.
Three clean sets of 15 on the lateral raise means the 25s are next.
